24.1.intro: Each way to pay has its own fee, payout speed and risk. The fee on the price page is rarely the whole cost.

steps.say: Download last month's payout reports from each provider (Shopify Payments, PayPal, buy now pay later).
steps.check: You have one report per provider.
steps.lost: Download your Shopify Payments report.

steps.say: For each provider, divide total fees by the sales it handled. Example: $180 ÷ $9,000 = 2%.
steps.check: You have a real fee rate per provider.
steps.lost: Fees ÷ sales.

steps.say: Add hidden costs: currency conversion when you withdraw, fixed per-order fees on small orders, and fees kept on refunds.
steps.check: Your fee rates include everything.
steps.lost: Add the currency fee if you have one.

steps.say: Enter your blended fee rate (all fees ÷ all sales) in Helix as payment fees.
steps.check: Helix profit uses your real fees.
steps.lost: Enter one fee rate in Helix.

steps.say: Keep the methods customers use. Drop any method under about 2% of orders that costs much more than cards.
steps.check: Your payment list is lean.
steps.careful: Australia: buy now pay later often lifts order value, but its fee is several times a card fee. US: compare Shop Pay Installments fees with your margin before pushing them.
steps.lost: Remove one rarely used, pricey method.

steps.say: Check each provider's fee page once a year.
steps.check: Fee rises never surprise you.
steps.lost: Put a yearly reminder in your calendar.

24.2.intro: A payment provider can hold some of your money if it sees risk. A hold in the busy season could stop you paying suppliers.

steps.say: Read each provider's rules on holds and reserves (money held back for a while in case of refunds), once.
steps.check: You know what causes a hold.
steps.lost: Read Shopify Payments' hold rules.

steps.say: Before a big sale or launch, tell your providers the dates and expected sales.
steps.check: A planned spike is less likely to cause a hold.
steps.lost: Email your provider your sale dates.

steps.say: Add tracking to every order within a day.
steps.check: Held money is released faster because orders show as delivered.
steps.lost: Add tracking to today's orders.

steps.say: Show honest delivery times. State pre-order ship dates clearly.
steps.check: Customers know when to expect orders.
steps.lost: Add a ship date to pre-orders.

steps.say: Keep at least one month of costs in cash, and a second payment method ready to switch on.
steps.check: A hold can't stop the business.
steps.lost: Set up PayPal as a backup.

steps.say:
If money is held, give the provider everything in one go.

1. Ask exactly what they need (like tracking, invoices or ID).
2. Send it all in one reply.
3. Add a follow-up date to your Helix calendar.
steps.check: The hold is sorted as fast as possible.
steps.careful: Keep business details, bank account and ID up to date with every provider. Old details are a common cause of freezes.
steps.lost: Ask what they need. Send it all at once.

24.3.intro: A chargeback is when a customer asks their bank to reverse a card payment. The bank takes the money and a fee straight away. You have a short time to prove the sale was fine.

steps.say: Open the chargeback in Shopify. Note the deadline, usually 7 to 21 days on Shopify Payments.
steps.check: You know your deadline. Customers usually have about 120 days to dispute.
steps.lost: Write down the deadline.

steps.say: Read the reason: "not received", "not as described" or "fraudulent".
steps.check: You know what proof you need.
steps.lost: Find the reason word.

steps.say: For "not received", gather tracking that shows delivery to the address given, plus any messages confirming details.
steps.check: You have proof of delivery.
steps.lost: Save the tracking page.

steps.say: For "not as described", gather your product page at the time, photos, your returns policy, and messages offering a fix.
steps.check: You can show the product matched the listing.
steps.lost: Save a copy of the product page.

steps.say: For "fraudulent", gather proof the real cardholder ordered: matching billing and shipping address, past orders, and opened tracking emails.
steps.check: You have the best proof available. These are the hardest to win.
steps.lost: Check if billing and shipping match.

steps.say: Write a short, factual response with the strongest proof first. Submit it.
steps.check: It's submitted before the deadline.
steps.lost: Put your best proof first. Submit.

steps.say: Contact the customer politely. Many disputes are confusion they can withdraw.
steps.check: Some disputes are withdrawn.
steps.lost: Send one kind message.

steps.say: Track your chargeback rate (disputes ÷ orders) every month. Example: 2 ÷ 1,000 = 0.2%.
steps.check: You catch a rising rate before card networks penalise you.
steps.careful: For pricey orders, use signature on delivery. It's the strongest proof you can buy.
steps.lost: Disputes ÷ orders, once a month.

24.4.intro: Card testing is when fraudsters use your checkout to try stolen card numbers, usually with lots of tiny orders on your cheapest product.

steps.say: Learn the signs: bursts of small orders, the same cheap item, odd names or emails, lots of failed payments, or different addresses on one card.
steps.check: You can spot card testing.
steps.lost: Many tiny orders at once? That's a sign.

steps.say: Use your platform's protections: Shopify's fraud analysis and checkout bot protection.
steps.check: You know what Shopify already blocks.
steps.lost: Turn on bot protection.

steps.say: Read the fraud risk level on every order before shipping. Hold high-risk orders while you contact the customer.
steps.check: No high-risk order ships unchecked.
steps.lost: Check the risk level before you ship.

steps.say: Cancel and refund any order that looks like fraud before shipping.
steps.check: You pay a refund instead of a chargeback.
steps.lost: Looks fake? Cancel and refund.

steps.say: Turn on 3D Secure (an extra bank check at payment) where your provider allows, at least for high-risk orders.
steps.check: Risky payments get an extra check.
steps.lost: Turn on 3D Secure.

steps.say: If testing keeps happening, raise the minimum order or hide your cheapest product for a while.
steps.check: The attacks stop.
steps.careful: Be careful with gift cards, and very large first orders going to parcel forwarding addresses.
steps.lost: Hide your cheapest product for a week.

24.5.intro: A fast, fair refund is cheaper than a dispute. A clear rule means you don't decide each case from scratch.

steps.say: Write a one-page refund rule: when you refund in full, when you offer a part refund or credit, and who approves it.
steps.check: Your team can handle any refund the way you would.
steps.lost: Write when you give a full refund.

steps.say: For small problems, offer a fix first: a part refund or store credit if the customer keeps the item.
steps.check: Fewer full refunds.
steps.careful: Australia: refunds for faulty items are a legal right. Goodwill is extra. US: state law and your published policy set the rules.
steps.lost: Offer a part refund for a small problem.

steps.say: Always refund to the original payment method.
steps.check: No disputes from money sent another way.
steps.lost: Refund to the same card.

steps.say: Write down every refund reason.
steps.check: You can fix the cause.
steps.lost: Write the reason for this refund.

steps.say: Enter refunds in Helix.
steps.check: Profit stays true.
steps.lost: Enter this week's refunds.
